text:
H.  W.  Taylor  communicated  in  Cincinnati  Medical  Advance,  1878,  a  kind
of  poisoning  of  five  children  after  eating  freely  of  the  fruit.  The  symptoms
are  marked  t.


^  Mind.      Did  not  care  to  hold  conversation  with  any  one,  even  his
best  friends  ;  with  aching  in  lung.
Could  not  dismiss  from  his  mind  what  occurred  through  the
day  previous  ;  at  night.     See  37.
^  Inner  Head.     Frontal  headache,  with  pain  in  the  chest.
Frontal  headache,  with  nausea,,  t.

Did  not  rest  well  the  night  previous,  arose  with   an  unusual
headache  in  left  temporal  region,  involving  the  eye,  with  an
occasional  sharp  pain  over  it,  increased  by  a  single  cough.
On  morning  of  4th  day  headache  increased  ;  felt  uncomfortable
all  day  ;  stomach  felt  increased  in  size ;  insufficiency  of  stool ;
inactivity  of  the  bowels  and  rectum.
Headache,  with  chill,  nausea  and  belching.
''  Smell  and  Nose.      I  Discharge  from  the  nose  altered  in  charac-
ter from  yellow,  thick,  and  at  times,  especially  in  the  morn-
ing, hard,  flakey,  dark-gray  consistency,  at  times  offensive,
to  a  natural  mucous  secretion.
^  Face.     Face  turns  blue,  with  spasmodic  interruption  of  breath-
ing.    See  26.
^^  Inner  Mouth.     Corroding  sensation  in  mouth.

I  Aphthse  of  children.
"  Palate  and  Throat.     Soreness  of  throat ;  t.

Fauces  red,  swollen  ;  tonsils  and  submaxillary  glands  enlarged
next  day  ;  t.
"  Thirst,  Desires.     Thirst,  with  heat ;  drinks  much ;  desire  for

ice-cold  things.
"  Eating  and  Drinking.     Soon  after  eating,  a  loose  stool.
^^  Nausea,  Vomiting  and  Belching.    Nausea  and  belching.
Constant  belching.
Vomiting.


221  ASIMINA  TRILOBA.

^^  Scrobiculum  and  Stomach.     Stomach  felt  increased  in  size,
with  headache.
Soreness  on  pressure  in  region  of  stomach.
^^  Hypochondria.     Exercised  a  good  deal  through  the  day  ;  ex-
perienced a  pain  in  the  left  hypochondrium,  and  a  soreness
in  region  of  stomach  on  pressure.
^^  Abdomen,  Loins  and  Groins.     Soreness  in  abdomen  on  pres-
sure ;  slight  pain  resembling  colic.
Colic.

Sensation  of  distension  by  wind.
Rumbling  and  pain.
^^  Rectum  and  Stool.     Insufficiency  of  stool ;  inactivity  of  bow-
els and  rectum.     See  3.
Diarrhoea  after  eating.

Rumbling  pain  in  abdomen,  with  desire  for  stool,  which  re-
sulted in  the  passage  of  a  soft  pappy  insufficient  stool ;  in
the  evening.
»    Soreness  of  anus  when  wiping  it.

Sudden  urging  to  stool,  with  a  sensation  as  if  a  stick  the  thick-
ness of  a  thumb,  passed  down  the  rectum  ;  followed  by  a
sudden  diarrhoeical  stool,  repeating  every  10, 15  minutes,  with
chilliness,  drowsiness,  and  a  weak  voice.
Diarrhoea  of  yellowish  discharges  next  day  ;  t.
Diarrhoea  lasting  more  than  four  weeks  ;  t.
All  the  children  had  diarrhoea  a  long  time  after  other  symp-
toms had  disappeared ;  t.
^^  Urinary  Organs.     Urine  clear  as  water.
•  Diuretic.

Urging  to  urinate,  and  burning  when  urinating.
^'  Voice  and  Larynx.    Weak  voice.    See  20.
Quite  hoarse  in  the  morning.

1 1  Hoarseness,  requiring  much  effort  to  talk,  and  seeming  as
though  the  mucous  membrane  was  thickened  and  the  organs
slow  to  respond  to  the  effort  of  speech.
Throat  not  very  sore,  not  so  much  so  as  the  hoarseness  seemed
to  indicate  ;  slight  cough,  which  is  dry.
"  Respiration.     Talking  difficult.     See  25.

I  Cramp  in  the  chest  lasting  three  hours,  with  blueness  of  face.
^^  Cough.     A  single  cough  increased  the  pain  over  the  eye.

A  slight,  dry  cough.
^*  Inner  Chest  and  Lungs.     Dull,  aching  pain  in  upper  left  lung ;

headache  continuing.
^^  Outer  Chest.     Lower  end  of  sternum  sore  on  pressure.
^^  Neck  and  Back.     Chill  over  the  whole  back.

All  children  had  scarlet  eruption  on  neck  and  upper  limbs ;  t.
*^  Upper  Limbs.     Pain  in  left  shoulder,  seeming  to  involve  the

pectoral  muscles.
^^  Lower  Limbs.      Sharp  pain  in  left  hip-joint,  lasting  about  half

an  hour,  11|  a.m.,  returned  half-past  1  p.m.;  in  the  evening

other  pains  in  the  joint  more  mild  than  the  former,  lasting

Eruption  in  front,  below  the  knee,  like  nettles ;  itching  when

uncovering.
Carbuncle  on  anterior  aspect  of  1.  thigh ;  suppuration  lasting

two  weeks ;  t.
^^  Sleep.     Fever,  heat  with  sleepiness.     See  40.

Did  not  rest  well  night  previous,  kept  turning  and  moving  all

night;  could  not  dismiss  from  his  mind  what  had  occurred

through  the  day.
Got  up  feeling  unrefreshed ;  headache  no  better ;  quite  hoarse  ;

pain  in  left  shoulder.     See  32.
Drowsiness  and  sleeplessness  alternating.
^^  Time.     Morning :    headache    <  ;    hard   discharge    from   nose ;

hoarseness  ;  languid  and  pale.
11.30  A.M.  and  1.30  p.m.  :  pain  in  left  hip-joint.
Evening  :  diarrhoeic  stool ;  pain  in  left  hip-joint  slight.
^^  Temperature  and  Weather.    Uncovering  knee  :  itching  worse.
Open  air  :  exercise  in  open  air  is  followed  by  relief  of  headache.
*'  Chill.    Fever.    Sweat.     Chill.    See  3  and  31.
Chilliness.     See  20.
Heat  with  thirst.
Fever  heat :  with  desire  for  something  icy  cold ;  with  drowsiness  ;

with  much  thirst.
Chill  over  the  back.
*^  Locality  and  Direction.     Aching  in  chest  more  on  left  than

on  right  side.
Left :  headache  temporal  region  ;  pain  in  hypochondrium  ;  pain

in  upper  lung  ;  pain  in  shoulder  ;  pain  in  hip-joint ;  carbun-
cle on  thigh.
Left  to  right :    eruptions  appeared  in  provers  first  left   then

right.
*^  Sensations.     As  of  a  stick  in  rectum.

Sharp  pain  :  over  1.  eye ;  in  1.  hip-joint.
Corroding :  in  mouth.

Soreness  :  in  throat ;  in  stomach  ;  in  abdomen  ;  of  anus.
Dull  aching  :  in  upper  1.  lung.
Cramp  :  in  chest.

Undefined  pain :  in  chest;  in  1.  hypochondrium ;  in  1.  shoulder.
*'*  Touch.     Passive    Motion.     Injuries.     Pressure :    soreness

in  epigastrium  and  abdomen ;  lower  end  of  sternum  sore.
Wiping :  anus  sore.
*®  Skin.     Itching  red  pimples.

Pustules  like  small-pox,  with  a  red  halo,   itching,   and  after

scratching  forming  thick  crusts,  lasting  from   six  to   eight

weeks ;  t.
Itching  when  undressing  in  the  evening.


223  ASIM.  TR.— ASPAR.

Abscesses  ripening.

Eruption  first  on  left  then  on  right  side.

Nettle-rash.

10  P.M. :  violent  fever;  had  vomited,  and  was  covered  with  a
bright  scarlet  eruption  ;  pulse  130,  full  and  steady ;  tempera-
ture 105 ;  t.

General  desquamation  followed ;  t.
*^  Relationship.     Collateral  relations :   the  Anonacese,  of  which
the  Asim.  fr.  is  the  only  one  proved,  although  a  very  impor-
tant family.

Compare  :  lllic.  anis.  (colic) ;  Liriodendron.

The  skin  of  the  fruit  and  the  seeds  are  fetid,  somewhat  similar
to  Stramon.


ASPARAGUS  OFFICINALIS.

Asparagus.  Liliacecp..

Introduced  and  proved  in  1840  by  Buchner,  who  proved  the  sprouts;
later  others  made  provings.  Jeanes  proved  the  root.  The  strongest  effect
must  be  obtained  from  the  berries,  and  still  more  from  the  seed.  Many-
symptoms  may  be  added  by  practitioners  if  they  meet  with  cases  in  which
asparagus  disagrees.

^  Mind.     Cheerfulness ;  serenity  of  mind  ;  the  5th  day.
A  peculiar  anxiety,  with  palpitation  and  ill  humor.
Fretful  and  peevish,  disturbed  by  trifles  ;  constant  anxiety  and
apprehension.
"^  Sensorium.     Vertigo  :  slight  in  the  afternoon ;  in  the  forehead ;
with  staggering.
Confusion  of  the  head.
Dullness  of  the  head.
'  Inner  Head.     Dizziness  in  forehead,  afterwards  aching  in  tem-
ples, especially  the  left.
Aching  in  forehead,  with  confusion.
Pressing  pains  in  both  temples,  worse  from  pressure.
Heaviness,  pressure  in  forehead,  the  pain  presses  towards  the
eyes.
^  Sight  and  Eyes.     Increased  acuteness  of  vision.
Stitches  and  tickling  in  the  eyes.
Aching  of  the  brain  near  the  eyes.
Pains  in  the  eyeballs.
Drawing  pain  over  eyebrows  all  across.

^  Smell  and  Nose.      I  l  Frequent  sneezing ;    after  smelling    the
tincture.

Corjza,  with  slight  dryness  and  swelling  inside,  then  impeded
entrance  of  air ;  gets  violent  with  frequent  discharge  of  a
thin  white  fluid  from  1.  nostril ;  irritation  to  sneeze,  and  fre-
quent sneezing.

Later  with  the  catarrh  a  pressing  pain  from  root  of  nose  to  fore-
head;  next  day,  at  9  a.m.,  dry  coryza  ;  later  running  ;  want
of  smell ;  violent  sneezing ;  the  3d  day  discharge  of  mucus
from  the  r.  nostril.
"  Face.     Increased  heat  of  the  face.

Burning  of  the  cheeks.

■  Countenance  pale,  wax- like  and  hloated.

■  General  expression  of  anxiety  and  distress.     See  29.

^^  Teeth  and  Gums.     Painless  cavity ;  exfoliation  of  a  carious
molar.

■  Relieved  toothache.

*^  Taste,    Tongue.     Taste :   sweetish,    insipid ;    coppery ;    bitter-
sweetish  on  the  tongue.
Smarting  feeling  on  the  tongue.
^^  Inner    Mouth.      Saliva  increased  ;    sweetish,  as  if  mixed  with

blood;  diminished;  later  more  copious.
'^  Palate  and  Throat.     Almost  constant  hawking,  with  a  rough
feeling  in  the  throat.
Copious  discharge  of  tenacious  mucus  from  the  throat.

■  Deglutition  difficult.     ^Hydrophobia.

■  Burning  in  the  throat.

Feeble  appetite.
*  Eating   and   Drinking.     After  breakfast :    cough   remitted ;
pain  in  chest.
After  eating  :  palpitation.     See  29.
Fullness  and  oppression  after  eating  or  drinking.

^^  Belching,  Nausea  and  Vomiting.    Belching  of  wind.

Nausea  5  a.m.,  on  awaking;  vomited  the  food  taken  the  even-
ing before,  with  bile  and  much  mucus,  followed  by  a  bilious
diarrhoea;  after  15  minutes  another  attack  of  difficult  vomit-

Retching  bringing  tears  into  the  eyes,  when  attempting  to  cough.

Nausea  after  each  exertion.
^''  Scrobiculum  and  Stomach.     Pain  in  region  of  cardiac  end  of

^^  Abdomen,  Loins  and  Groins.     Sense  of  fullness  in  abdomen.

Griping  in  region  of  navel,  which  is  painful  when  touched.

Drawing  pains  in  both  groins.
^^  Rectum  and  Stool.     Discharge  of  much  wind.

Insufficient  stool  in  afternoon,  notwithstanding  a  regular  stool
in  morning.

Bilious  diarrhoea,  with  colic.

A  peculiar  urging,  with  difficult,  hard  fecal  discharge ;  haemor-
rhoids bleed  much  more.

Burning  and  soreness  at  the  anus.

Nephritic  colic.

Urging  to  urinate ;  evening  1st  day.

Urging  to  urinate ;  urine  of  a  tolerably  strong  odor.

Frequent  scanty  discharge  preceded  by  a  sensation  as  if

■  Relieved  prurigo  pudendi  in  women,  aet.  40.

Spitting  blood.

While  walking,  pain  as  from  dislocation  in  the  neck  of  the  right

Compelled  to  throw  chest  forward  and  head  backward  to  find

Very  much  prostrated,  pulse  irregular.     See  48.

Sleep  uneasy  and  disturbed  by  oppressed  breathing.
